No legal prohibitions to prevent states adopting distinctive flags exist in either the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950 or the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/should-states-have-their-own-flags/article22695446.ece|title=Should States have their own flags?|website=The Hindu|date=9 February 2018|access-date=12 September 2019}} In a 1994 case before the [[Supreme Court of India]], ''[[S. R. Bommai v. Union of India]]'', the Supreme Court declared that there is no prohibition in the Constitution of India for a state to have its own flag. However, a state flag should not dishonour the national flag.{{Cite web|url = https://www.sundayguardianlive.com/news/non-nda-states-playing-emblem-politics-cover-failure|title = 'Non-NDA states playing emblem politics to cover up their failure'|date = 14 July 2018|access-date = 22 March 2020|archive-date = 22 March 2020|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200322151052/https://www.sundayguardianlive.com/news/non-nda-states-playing-emblem-politics-cover-failure|url-status = dead}} The [[Flag code of India]] also permits other flags to be flown with the [[Flag of India]], but not on the same flag pole or in a superior position to the national flag.{{cite web|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Flag_Code_of_India|title=Flag Code of India - Wikisource, the free online library|website=en.wikisource.org|access-date=12 September 2019}} === Former official state flags === The state of [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]] had an officially recognised state flag between 1952 and 2019 under the special status granted to the state by [[Article 370 of the Constitution of India]]. {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! class="unsortable" style="width:100px;" |Flag !! class="unsortable" style="width:75px;" |State !! style="width:100px;" |Usage date !! The red background stood for labour and the plough stood for agriculture.
